description: I1 SAML cert substitution: control login with trusted CA-based signature validation, then attempt attacker-signed forged assertion; acceptance indicates signature verification not applied to consumed proof.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must reject SAML assertions not signed by the configured trusted IdP certificate (CA/caData).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control SAML login failed; cannot attribute attack acceptance/rejection to signature validation behavior.
Dex accepted an attacker-signed forged SAML assertion even though signature validation was configured with a trusted CA/cert.

description: I1 policy confusion check: first configure connector to skip signature validation (expected accept), then reconfigure to enforce validation and retry same forged login (must reject). Acceptance after reconfig indicates verification policy not applied to consumed proof.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: When signature validation is enabled, Dex must not accept attacker-signed assertions; behavior must change when toggling insecureSkipSignatureValidation from true to false.

oracle_checks.violation_description: In insecureSkipSignatureValidation=true mode, forged assertion should be accepted by configuration; rejection suggests the test did not exercise the intended path.
After reconfiguring to enforce signature validation, Dex still accepted attacker-signed forged SAML assertion (verification policy not applied to consumed proof).

description: SAML signature enforcement toggle: prove that when signature validation is enabled, attacker-signed assertions are rejected (and only accepted when insecureSkipSignatureValidation=true).
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must apply signature verification to the exact SAML assertion it consumes; attacker-signed assertions must be rejected under signature-validation configuration.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted an attacker-signed SAML assertion even though signature validation was configured (CA provided, insecureSkipSignatureValidation=false).
Sanity placeholder: acceptance under insecureSkipSignatureValidation=true is by configuration and must not be treated as an I1 finding.

description: SAML response-wrapping style test: attempt to swap the consumed principal (NameID) while keeping issuer/audience seemingly valid; detect if Dex consumes a different semantic assertion than it verifies.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must verify and consume the same semantic SAML assertion; it must not accept a response where the verified signature covers different content than the assertion used for identity (wrapping/nameid swap).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a potentially wrapped/swapped SAML assertion where the consumed principal could differ from the verified content (signature-wrapping class).
Dex mapped attacker and victim-like NameIDs to the same downstream identity during a wrapping-style attempt, suggesting proof/subject confusion.

description: I1/I3-adjacent proof-integrity check: attempt to splice a SAMLResponse generated for one SP-initiated AuthnRequest into a different session's callback (cross-session InResponseTo confusion). If accepted, Dex may be verifying one semantic proof but consuming it under a different session context.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must apply authenticity checks to the exact semantic proof bound to the initiating AuthnRequest/session; a SAMLResponse for session A must not be accepted/consumed in session B.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a SAMLResponse spliced into a different SP-initiated session (proof verified/consumed under wrong session context).

description: Replay the exact same SAML Assertion/@ID across two SP-initiated sessions, changing NameID/email to simulate cross-principal replay. Second submission must be rejected if Dex tracks assertion IDs.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: A SAML assertion artifact (Assertion/@ID) must be one-time; reusing the same assertion ID in a later session must be rejected even if other attributes differ.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control SAML login did not succeed; replay test is inconclusive due to broken setup/flow.
Dex accepted a replayed SAML assertion with the same Assertion/@ID in a later session (replay not detected).

description: Replay the exact same SAML Assertion/@ID twice within the same SP-initiated session (same RelayState) to test whether Dex enforces one-time consumption of the assertion artifact.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: A SAML assertion artifact (Assertion/@ID) must not be accepted more than once, even if replayed immediately within the same SP-initiated session context.

oracle_checks.violation_description: SP-initiated SAML flow did not start successfully; replay result would be inconclusive.
Control SAML login did not succeed; replay result would be inconclusive.
Dex accepted the same SAML Assertion/@ID twice within the same SP-initiated session (replay not prevented).

description: Obtain a SAML login, revoke the resulting session token, then attempt to replay the same SAML Assertion/@ID in a new SP-initiated flow. Revoke should not make the original assertion reusable.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Revoking a session must not reset anti-replay state for previously-consumed SAML assertions; the same Assertion/@ID must still be rejected on replay.

oracle_checks.violation_description: First SP-initiated SAML flow did not start; test is inconclusive.
Control SAML login did not succeed; replay-after-revoke test is inconclusive.
Session revoke failed; cannot interpret replay-after-revoke behavior.
Second SP-initiated SAML flow did not start; replay-after-revoke test is inconclusive.
Dex accepted a replayed SAML Assertion/@ID after revoking the prior session, indicating replay state is not enforced or is incorrectly tied to session lifetime.

description: Control SAML login succeeds, then change connector audience expectation (entityIssuer override) and attempt an expired assertion login. Expired assertion must still be rejected regardless of config changes.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: SAML assertion time validity (NotOnOrAfter) must be enforced consistently and must not be bypassable after connector configuration changes and re-authentication.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control SP-initiated SAML flow did not start; expired-assertion test is inconclusive.
Control SAML login did not succeed; expired-assertion test is inconclusive.
Attack SP-initiated SAML flow did not start; expired-assertion test is inconclusive.
Dex accepted an expired SAML assertion (NotOnOrAfter in the past) after connector config change, indicating missing/incorrect time validity enforcement.

description: Replay the same SAML Assertion/@ID across two SP-initiated sessions, but between attempts delete/recreate the connector to test whether replay cache is improperly scoped to connector instance lifetime.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: SAML assertion IDs must not become reusable after connector recreation; replay protection must survive connector lifecycle changes.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Initial login failed; cannot evaluate replay-after-recreate behavior.
Dex accepted a replayed SAML assertion ID after connector recreation (replay cache improperly reset/scoped).

description: First login uses OneTimeUse assertion; revoke resulting session token; then attempt to reuse the same OneTimeUse assertion ID in a new SP-initiated flow as a different identity.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: OneTimeUse assertions must remain non-reusable regardless of downstream session revocation; revoking a session must not make the original SAML artifact reusable.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control OneTimeUse login failed; cannot interpret replay-after-revoke result.
Dex accepted a replayed OneTimeUse SAML assertion after session revocation (artifact became reusable).

description: Control SAML login succeeds, then attempt an expired assertion (should be rejected). If rejected, try replaying the exact same expired assertion ID in a fresh SP-initiated flow to detect any cache/TTL confusion that could allow reuse of expired artifacts.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: A SAML assertion that is expired (NotOnOrAfter in the past) must never be accepted, and re-submitting the same expired assertion artifact (same Assertion/@ID) in a new SP-initiated flow must also be rejected (no replay/TTL confusion).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control SAML login did not succeed; cannot interpret expired/replay results
Dex accepted an expired SAML assertion (NotOnOrAfter in the past) — freshness enforcement failure
Dex accepted a replay of the same expired SAML assertion ID in a new SP-initiated flow — anti-replay/TTL confusion

description: Cross-session splicing attempt: start two SP-initiated SAML auth flows, then submit a SAMLResponse bound to flow-A into flow-B callback context (RelayState swap). Expect rejection if Dex binds response to the correct session/request.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Dex must bind SAMLResponse (InResponseTo/RelayState) to the correct SP-initiated session; cross-session splicing must be rejected.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a SAMLResponse spliced into a different SP-initiated session (RelayState/InResponseTo binding failure).

description: Mid-flight connector mutation: start SP-initiated SAML flow, then delete and recreate the connector with same connector_id before posting SAMLResponse. Response should be rejected if Dex binds the flow to connector instance/config and prevents step-skipping across connector lifetimes.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: SP-initiated SAML flow must be atomic and bound to the connector instance/config that issued the AuthnRequest; deleting/recreating the connector mid-flow must not allow completion.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a SAMLResponse for a flow whose connector was deleted/recreated mid-flight (flow not atomic / connector-instance binding failure).

description: Client-binding confusion: create two OAuth clients with different redirect_uris. Start SAML auth for client-A, then attempt to complete SAML callback and exchange code using client-B redirect_uri. Expect rejection if auth code/session is bound to the initiating client and redirect_uri.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization code and SAML login completion must be bound to the initiating client_id and redirect_uri; cross-client/redirect_uri splicing must be rejected.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex allowed completing SAML login / exchanging code using a different client_id/redirect_uri than the one that initiated the flow (client/session splicing).

description: Attempt to skip SP-initiated step: POST a forged SAMLResponse to /callback without first calling /auth (no AuthnRequest/InResponseTo binding). Expect Dex to reject.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Dex must enforce SP-initiated flow ordering and reject SAML callbacks that are not bound to a prior /auth-initiated AuthnRequest (no step skipping).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a SAMLResponse without a prior /auth-initiated AuthnRequest (step skipping / missing InResponseTo binding).

description: Start SAML auth for client A, complete SAML login, then attempt to exchange the resulting code using a mismatched redirect_uri (client binding / redirect_uri coherence).
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization code issuance and redemption must be bound to the initiating client and redirect_uri; cross-client or wrong-redirect exchange must be rejected.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex allowed authorization code redemption with a different client_id/redirect_uri than the one that initiated the /auth request (cross-client splicing).

description: Start SP-initiated SAML flow, then change connector expected issuer (ssoIssuer) before posting SAMLResponse. Response should be rejected if flow is coherently bound to the initiating connector config/state.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: A multi-step SAML flow must be atomic and bound to the connector configuration at initiation; mid-flight config changes must not allow completing an earlier flow under a different policy.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a SAMLResponse for a flow initiated under issuer-A after the connector was reconfigured to issuer-B mid-flight (flow not atomic / config-splicing possible).

description: Cross-client flow splicing: start two SP-initiated SAML auth flows for different clients, then attempt to complete the callback using the wrong RelayState (client/session mix-up).
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Dex must bind the SAMLResponse completion to the initiating /auth request context (client_id/redirect_uri/state) and reject cross-client RelayState splicing.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a SAMLResponse completed with a RelayState from a different client/session (cross-client flow splicing).

description: Cross-identity splicing: start two SP-initiated SAML flows, then attempt to complete flow-A using flow-B's RelayState while asserting a different NameID/email. Should be rejected if response is bound to the correct request/session.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Dex must prevent cross-session splicing where a SAMLResponse for one browser/session is accepted under another session's RelayState, even if both are for the same client.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a SAMLResponse under a different session's RelayState while changing asserted principal attributes, indicating flow/session splicing.

description: I3 flow coherence: attempt to reuse (replay) the same SP-initiated SAML callback context (RelayState) to authenticate a second time without starting a new /auth flow. Expect Dex to reject the second callback because the flow should be one-shot and order-preserving.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: The SAML SP-initiated flow must be atomic and one-shot; a callback context (RelayState/InResponseTo binding) must not be reusable to complete a second login without a fresh /auth initiation.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a second SAML callback using the same RelayState without a fresh /auth initiation, indicating flow non-atomicity / step re-use (flow coherence violation).
Control SAML login did not succeed; cannot attribute second-step behavior to flow coherence enforcement.

description: Case confusion in SAML NameID: 'Admin' vs 'admin' should map to distinct downstream identities (no case-folding collision).
invariant_hypothesis: I4: Distinct upstream principals (NameID differing only by case) must not collapse into the same downstream subject.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Case-folding collision: NameID 'Admin' and 'admin' mapped to the same downstream identity

description: Email-binding collision attempt: keep NameID constant but change email to victim@example.com; downstream identity must remain bound to NameID (not rebind/merge by email).
invariant_hypothesis: I4: Downstream subject must remain bound to the upstream principal key (SAML NameID) and must not collapse/merge based on mutable attributes like email.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Account linking/collision: attacker NameID with victim email mapped to victim's downstream identity (email-based merge)
Unexpected principal rebinding: same NameID produced a different downstream identity when only email changed

description: I4 empty-sub/NameID: attempt to authenticate two distinct upstream principals where one has an empty NameID; ensure Dex does not collapse empty/blank NameID into another user's identity.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: Distinct upstream principals (NameID='userA' vs NameID='') must not map to the same downstream identity; empty NameID must not alias an existing subject.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Empty NameID was accepted and collapsed into an existing downstream identity (principal binding failure)

description: I4 cross-protocol identity merge: authenticate one user via password (if enabled) and another via SAML with same email but different NameID; ensure Dex does not merge identities across protocols based on email.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: A SAML principal (NameID) must not be merged into an existing local/password principal solely due to matching email; distinct upstream principals must map to distinct downstream identities.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
SAML principal was merged with local/password principal based on email (principal binding failure)

description: Config-change principal collision: change nameIDPolicyFormat between logins and see if two distinct NameIDs collapse to same downstream identity (should remain distinct).
invariant_hypothesis: I4: Even across connector config changes, distinct upstream NameIDs must not be mapped to the same downstream identity (no canonicalization/rewriting that collapses principals).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Distinct NameIDs across a connector nameIDPolicyFormat change collapsed to the same downstream identity

description: SAML control login succeeds, then attempt SAML login with Conditions removed (no audience/time bounds). If accepted, Dex grants a session without upstream intent constraints.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Dex must not grant an authenticated session when the SAML assertion omits Conditions (no audience/time bounds), because EffectivePerms would not be bounded by UpstreamIntent ∩ BrokerPolicy.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control SAML login failed; cannot interpret no-conditions result (setup may be broken).
Dex accepted a SAML assertion without Conditions (no audience/time bounds), violating authorization binding.

description: Obtain a subject_token via SAML for client valence-test-client, then attempt RFC8693 token exchange requesting an audience that should not be granted. Exchange should be rejected or not broaden effective permissions.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Token exchange must not allow a subject_token minted for one audience/context to be exchanged into a token for a different audience without explicit authorization; otherwise EffectivePerms can exceed UpstreamIntent ∩ BrokerPolicy.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control SAML login failed; cannot interpret token exchange behavior.
Dex token exchange accepted a subject_token to mint a token for an unrelated audience, violating authorization binding.

description: Control SAML login succeeds with correct audience (entityIssuer override), then attacker submits assertion with wrong AudienceRestriction to test audience binding enforcement.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Dex must enforce SAML AudienceRestriction against the configured expected audience (entityIssuer overrides redirectURI); a token/session must not be issued when the assertion audience does not match broker policy.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control SAML login failed; cannot evaluate audience-binding enforcement reliably.
Dex accepted a SAML assertion with an AudienceRestriction that does not match the configured expected audience (entityIssuer override), violating authorization binding.

description: Config change + re-auth: first configure connector without entityIssuer (audience defaults to redirectURI) and perform control login; then reconfigure with entityIssuer and attempt login with assertion still targeting old audience to ensure policy change is enforced.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: After a broker policy change (expected audience changes via entityIssuer), Dex must enforce the new audience binding and not accept assertions scoped to the previous audience.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Pre-change control login failed; cannot evaluate enforcement across config change.
After changing expected audience via entityIssuer, Dex still accepted an assertion scoped to the old audience (redirectURI), violating authorization binding under updated broker policy.

description: I5 audience binding under config change: first login with redirectURI-based audience; then reconfigure entityIssuer override and ensure old-audience assertions are rejected (no stale audience acceptance).
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Effective permissions must be bounded by current BrokerPolicy(config). After changing expected audience (entityIssuer override), Dex must not accept assertions targeting the previous audience (redirectURI).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control login before config change failed; cannot evaluate audience-binding behavior across reconfiguration
Dex accepted SAML login after audience policy change when it should have rejected assertions targeting the previous audience, indicating audience-binding/policy-staleness over-grant
